Voluble

VOL-yuh-bul · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Voluble is talking energetically and continuously; fluent and rapid in speech.

The voluble cab driver told three life stories before they'd even left the airport.

Worked Example

Once the topic turned to sailing, the usually quiet mechanic became surprisingly voluble.

The mechanic didn't just say a bit more -- he launched into a fluent, nonstop stream of talk, which is exactly voluble.

How Voluble Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

talkative

talkative: inclined to talk a great deal

garrulous

garrulous: excessively talkative, often about unimportant things

Antonyms

taciturn

taciturn: reserved and reluctant to speak

How Strong Is It? — chatty → voluble → unstoppable

chatty vs. voluble

chatty vs. voluble: Being chatty is mildly talkative and friendly; being voluble means talking nonstop, rapidly, and almost impossible to interrupt.

unstoppable vs. voluble

unstoppable vs. voluble: A voluble talker can occasionally be interrupted; an unstoppable one truly cannot be.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of voluble.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — volu

root — volu: to roll (Latin (volvere))

suffix — -ble

suffix — -ble: able to be (Latin (-ibilis))

Put it together

Put it together: Voluble comes from Latin volvere, 'to roll,' plus -ible -- so voluble originally meant words 'rolling' easily and rapidly off the tongue.

Use the root in a new word: revolve

Use the root in a new word: revolve: The same volvere root gives us revolve (to roll around and around) and evolve (to roll outward, gradually unfolding).

Root Check

Word Choice

Voluble is about the rate and fluency of speech (nonstop, rapid, hard to interrupt). You already met its two closest cousins in this course: garrulous (recent, meaning talkative to a tiresome degree) and taciturn (several units back, its natural opposite -- reserved and reluctant to speak). Voluble is also distinct from this unit's Petulance, which is a mood rather than a speech style.
